source: Written by Claude (claude-opus-5-5) from the county counts (AP via The New York Times), the 2024 baseline and Census ACS 2023 context.

24025.t:
In the governor's race, Harford County backed Cox over Moore by 13 points, 57,874 votes to 44,102. That is about 1 point closer than Trump's 14-point win here in 2024, a move toward the Democrats that matches the typical Maryland county and is a little smaller than the state's 3-point shift. Nationally, the typical county moved 14 points left. Among similar Maryland counties, Calvert moved 1 point left, St. Mary's 3 points left and Dorchester 5 points right.

Only 106,265 votes were cast, 71% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. With 93.8% of the expected vote counted, the numbers may still move.

24037.t:
St. Mary's County voted for Cox over Moore in the race for Maryland governor, 22,452 to 16,597, a Republican margin of 14 points. That is 3 points less Republican than Trump's 17-point margin over Harris in 2024, about the same shift as the state as a whole and more than the typical Maryland county's 1 point, ranking 8th of 24. Nationally the typical county moved 14 points toward the Democrats. Among similar counties, Calvert moved 1 point left, Washington 9 left and Worcester 2 right.

Only 40,913 votes were cast, 70% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. With 94.6% of the expected vote counted, the numbers may still move.

24017.t:
In the governor's race, Charles County backed Moore over Cox by 48 points, 48,153 to 15,872, up from Harris's 41-point margin in 2024. That 8-point shift toward the Democrats ranks fourth among Maryland's 24 counties, well beyond the state's 3-point move and the typical Maryland county's 1 point, though short of the typical 14-point move nationally. Among comparable counties, Montgomery moved 10 points left, Howard 5, and Baltimore County 1 point right.

Only 66,735 votes were cast, 73% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. With 93% of the expected vote counted, the numbers may still move.

24011.t:
In the race for Maryland governor, Caroline County moved slightly against the statewide tide. Republican Cox carried it 7,759 to 3,319 over Democrat Moore, a margin of about 39 points, compared with Trump's 38-point win here in 2024. That is a shift of less than a point toward the Republicans, while Maryland as a whole moved about 3 points toward the Democrats and the typical county nationally moved 14 points left.

Turnout fell to 11,525 votes, 71% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Among similar Maryland counties, Queen Anne's moved by the same small amount toward the Republicans, Cecil edged a point left, and Allegany moved about 7 points left.

24015.t:
Cecil County barely moved in the race for governor. Trump carried it by 31 points in 2024; Cox led Moore here by 30 points, 19,923 votes to 10,399, a shift of 1 point toward the Democrats. That is close to the typical Maryland county, which moved 1 point left, and far short of the national typical move of 14 points. Among similar counties, Queen Anne's and Carroll moved slightly right, while Washington swung 9 points left.

Only 31,534 votes have been cast so far, 60% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. With about 87% of the expected vote counted, the numbers may still move.

24041.t:
Talbot County split almost exactly evenly between Harris and Trump in 2024. In the governor's race it went to Cox over Moore by 2 points, 8,924 to 8,523, a move of 2 points toward the Republicans. That runs against Maryland as a whole, which moved 3 points toward the Democrats, and against the nation, where the typical county moved 14 points left. It ranks 21st of Maryland's 24 counties by move. Neighboring Kent moved 4 points right, while Wicomico and Calvert moved 2 and 1 points left.

Turnout was 17,935 votes, 79% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. With 94% of the expected vote counted, the numbers may still move.

24013.t:
In the governor's race, Carroll County moved about 2 points toward the Republicans, going against the statewide current. Cox led Moore 43,484 to 24,392, a margin of 27 points, compared with Trump's 25-point margin in 2024. Moore carried Maryland by 31 points, and 15 of its 24 counties moved left. Carroll ranks 20th by move, close to Worcester, which also shifted 2 points right, while Washington swung 9 points toward the Democrats.

Only 70,642 votes were cast, 69% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. With 93% of the expected vote counted, the numbers may still move.

24023.t:
In the governor's race, Dan Cox carried Garrett County over Wes Moore by 7,909 votes to 2,432, a margin of 51 points. That is 3 points narrower than Donald Trump's 54-point win over Kamala Harris here in 2024, the same shift toward the Democrats as Maryland as a whole. The move ranks ninth among the state's 24 counties, where the typical county shifted 1 point left. Nationally, the typical county moved 14 points left.

Only 10,671 votes were cast, 68% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Among similar counties, Allegany moved 7 points left, Cecil 1 point left and Caroline 1 point right.

24005.t:
In the race for governor, Moore (D) leads Cox (R) in Baltimore County 154,051 to 93,118, a margin of 24 points, with about 82% of the expected vote counted, so the numbers may still move. Harris carried the county by 25 points in 2024, making this a shift of 1 point toward the Republicans. The state as a whole moved 3 points toward the Democrats.

That puts Baltimore County 18th of Maryland's 24 counties by move. Fifteen counties moved left, the typical one by about 1 point. Among similar counties, Anne Arundel moved 1 point left, Howard 5 and Frederick 8. So far 258,935 votes are counted, 63% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

24035.t: In the governor's race, Queen Anne's County voted for Republican Dan Cox over Democrat Wes Moore by 28 points, 14,980 to 8,178. That is almost exactly Donald Trump's 28-point margin here in 2024, a shift of less than a point toward the Republicans. Statewide, Moore won by 32 points, about 3 points better than Kamala Harris did. Queen Anne's ranked 17th of Maryland's 24 counties by move. The typical county shifted about 1 point left, and nationally the typical county shifted 14. Similar counties split, with Cecil moving 1 point left and Worcester and Carroll 2 points right. About 24,021 votes were cast, three-quarters of the 2024 total, so the count cannot separate changed minds from voters who stayed home. With 92% of the expected vote counted, the numbers may still move.

24009.t:
In the race for Maryland governor, Calvert County went to Cox over Moore, 20,024 votes to 16,242, a Republican margin of 10 points. That is 1 point better for Democrats than Trump's 11-point win over Harris here in 2024. The shift is about the same as the typical Maryland county's and smaller than the state's 3-point move. Nationally, the typical county moved 14 points left. Among similar Maryland counties, St. Mary's moved 3 points left and Harford 1.

The 37,775 votes counted so far equal 70% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. With 92% of the expected vote counted, the numbers may still move.

24047.t:
In the governor's race, Worcester County went for Cox over Moore by 24 points, 13,906 votes to 8,370. That is a little redder than its 22-point margin for Trump in 2024. The 2-point move toward the Republicans ran against the state, which moved 3 points toward the Democrats as Moore won by 32, and against the nation, where the typical county moved 14 points left. Worcester ranks 19th of Maryland's 24 counties by move. Similar counties split: Washington moved 9 points left, St. Mary's 3 left and Queen Anne's slightly right.

Only 23,076 votes were cast, 71% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. With about 91% of the expected vote counted, the numbers may still move.

24043.t:
In the race for Maryland governor between Moore and Cox, Washington County voted Republican, but by less than it did for president in 2024. Trump carried it by 23 points; Cox led by 14, 26,887 votes to 19,865, a shift of 9 points toward the Democrats. That was the second-largest move among Maryland's 24 counties, where the typical one moved 1 point. Similar counties went the other way or barely moved: Carroll and Worcester each moved 2 points right, and St. Mary's 3 points left. Nationally the typical county moved 14 points left.

Only 48,686 votes were cast, two-thirds of the 2024 total, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. With 93% of the expected vote counted, the numbers may still move.

24033.t:
In the race for Maryland governor, Prince George's County gave Moore 228,680 votes to Cox's 18,007, a Democratic margin of 82 points. That is 7 points more Democratic than the county's 75-point margin for Harris over Trump in 2024, more than double the state's 3-point shift and well above the typical Maryland county's 1-point move. It ranks fifth of 24 counties by shift. Nearby comparisons varied: Montgomery moved 10 points, Howard 5 and Baltimore 1.

Only 256,249 votes have been counted, 64% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. With about 79% of the expected vote in, the numbers may still move.

24019.t:
In the governor's race, Dorchester County moved toward the Republicans while Maryland moved the other way. Cox led Moore here by 19 points, 7,159 votes to 4,785, up from Trump's 15-point margin in 2024, a shift of about 5 points. Statewide, Moore won by 31, three points better than Harris. Only one of Maryland's 24 counties moved further right; nationally, 2,673 of 2,775 counted counties moved left.

Turnout was 74% of the 2024 vote, 12,452 ballots against 16,730, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Somerset, a similar county, moved about 6 points right, while St. Mary's and Calvert edged left. With 93% of the expected vote counted, the numbers may still move.

24031.t:
In the governor's race between Moore and Cox, Montgomery County gave Moore 262,549 votes to 55,992, a margin of D+63. That is 10 points more Democratic than Harris's D+53 in 2024, the largest move of Maryland's 24 counties, where the typical county moved about 1 point and the state moved 3. It also outpaced similar neighbors Prince George's (+7), Charles (+8) and Howard (+5), though it trailed the national typical move of 14 points.

Only 328,738 votes are in, 64% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. With about 79% of the expected vote counted, these numbers may still move.

24045.t:
In the governor's race, Republican Cox carried Wicomico County over Democrat Moore 15,799 to 14,715, a margin of about 3 points. Trump had won it by about 6 in 2024, so the county moved roughly 2 points toward the Democrats. That is a bit less than Maryland's 3-point shift but more than the typical Maryland county's 1 point, and well short of the typical 14-point leftward move nationally. Similar counties split: Calvert moved 1 point left, while Talbot and Kent moved 2 and 4 points right.

Only 31,893 votes were cast, 68% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. With about 91% of the expected vote counted, the numbers may still move.

24001.t:
In the race for Maryland governor, Allegany County stayed firmly Republican but swung about 7 points toward the Democrats. Cox led Moore 13,534 to 6,519, a margin of about 34 points, compared with Trump's 40-point win here in 2024. Only 20,833 votes were cast, 65% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. With about 92% of the expected vote counted, the numbers may still move.

The shift was larger than the state's 3-point move and the typical Maryland county's 1 point, ranking sixth of 24. Similar Republican counties barely budged: Caroline, Cecil and Queen Anne's each moved less than a point. Nationally, the typical county moved 14 points left.

24003.t:
In the governor's race between Moore and Cox, Anne Arundel County voted D+16, with Moore leading 122,103 to 87,268. That is about 2 points more Democratic than its D+14 margin for Harris in 2024. The shift is close to Maryland's statewide move of 3 points and a little above the typical Maryland county's 1 point, but far smaller than the typical 14-point leftward move nationally. Similar counties split: Frederick moved 8 points left, while Baltimore and Talbot moved about 1 and 2 points right.

About 218,100 votes have been counted, roughly 71% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. With 90% of the expected vote in, the numbers may still move.

24029.t:
In the governor's race between Moore and Cox, Kent County moved about 4 points toward the Republicans, from a 3-point Trump margin in 2024 to a 6-point Cox lead, 4,214 votes to 3,698. Statewide, Moore won by 32 points, 3 better than Harris. Kent ranks 22nd of Maryland's 24 counties by move, while nationally 2,673 of 2,775 counted counties moved left. Similar counties split: Talbot and Dorchester also moved right, by 2 and 5 points, while Wicomico moved 2 points left.

The 8,193 votes counted so far are 74% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. With 90% of the expected vote in, the numbers may still move.

24039.t:
In the governor's race between Moore and Cox, Somerset County moved about 6 points toward the Republicans. Trump carried it by 17 points in 2024; Cox leads it by 23, with 4,224 votes to Moore's 2,598. That is the largest rightward move of Maryland's 24 counties, while the state as a whole moved 3 points toward the Democrats and Moore won by 32. Nationally, the typical county moved 14 points left. Nearby Dorchester and Worcester also moved right, by 5 and 2, while St. Mary's moved 3 left.

Only 7,067 votes have been counted so far, 70% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. With about 91% of the expected vote in, the numbers may still move.

24510.t:
**Note to editor:** FIPS 24510 is Baltimore City, not Baltimore County (24005). A 2024 margin of D+73 also fits the city. Please confirm which one this is before publishing. The note below doesn't name the place, so it works either way.

In the governor's race between Moore and Cox, this jurisdiction went D+74, with 117,404 votes for the Democrat to 13,446 for the Republican. Harris carried it by 73 points in 2024, so the margin moved 1 point toward the Democrats. That is slightly more than the typical Maryland county (+1) but well short of similar places: Prince George's moved 7 points, Montgomery 10 and Howard 5.

Only 71% of the expected vote is counted, so these numbers may still move. Turnout so far is 61% of the 2024 total, and the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

24027.t:
In the governor's race, Howard County went for Moore over Cox 95,030 to 33,015, a Democratic margin of 46 points, up from Harris's 42-point margin in 2024. That 5-point move to the left beat Maryland's statewide shift of 3 points and ranks seventh of the state's 24 counties, where the typical county moved about 1 point. It fell short of the national typical move of 14 points and of similar counties Charles (8 points) and Montgomery (10), while Baltimore County moved 1 point right.

Only 133,827 votes were cast, 74% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. With 93% of the expected vote counted, the numbers may still move.

24021.t:
In the governor's race between Moore and Cox, Frederick County gave the Democrat an 18-point margin, 64,576 votes to 44,092, up from Harris's 9-point edge in 2024. That 9-point shift toward the Democrats is the second-largest among Maryland's 24 counties, well ahead of the typical state county (+1) and of the statewide move (about +4), though below the national typical move of +14. Similar counties moved less: Anne Arundel shifted 2 points left, Baltimore County did not move, and Talbot moved 2 points right.

Only 112,858 votes were cast, 73% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. With 94% of the expected vote counted, the numbers may still move.
